_doc: Latency budgets for the engine's own nightly-measurable benchmarks (Phase 66). Each budget names its owner criterion group/id under crates/krishiv-bench/benches/ so scripts/bench-tier.sh knows where to read target/criterion/<path>/new/estimates.json. The gate (scripts/bench_gate.py, ported from the platform repo's Phase 29) flags results exceeding budget by >20% on two consecutive nightly runs. Units: milliseconds unless noted. TPC-H budgets are declared under `"tier": "tpch"` and are evaluated ONLY by `scripts/bench-tpch-tier.sh --tier tpch` on a host that has the dataset; the nightly job passes `--tier nightly` so `--require-fresh` never fails on them. `"tier": "datasets"` budgets cover the two targets CI provisions its own SF1 data for (tpch_distributed via tpchgen-cli, tpcds_smoke via scripts/bench/gen_tpcds_sf1.py) — run nightly by scripts/bench-datasets-tier.sh from bench.yml's dataset-tier job with `--tier datasets`. tpch_sf10 and tpch_overhead still need multi-GB pre-generated data that CI does not provision, so they self-skip (see BENCHMARKING.md's 'What this gate does not cover yet') rather than being declared here and permanently failing --require-fresh for an infrastructure reason, not a performance one.
